why: The named, shrink-only record of every check `make verify` is allowed to record as SKIP (rc 2 CANNOT-ASSESS) -- scripts/verify.sh's skip ratchet (issue #1199). A skip is named here or the run is REFUSED by name: the composite will not publish a `verify: PASS` whose skip set is narrated by nobody. Two kinds, both precise: `venue` (the check cannot assess because a NAMED PRECONDITION this venue must supply is not supplied -- honoured only while it is NOT supplied, so it de-activates itself the moment the venue supplies it; a check that still cannot assess WITH its precondition supplied is a defect of the CHECK, #1176, and is refused by name). A venue precondition has exactly TWO measured forms, never an assertion: a repo-relative PATH that must be absent (`vendor/CMR/sync`), and a COMMAND this venue must be able to run (`gh auth status`, supplied only when the command exits 0). The command form is the check's OWN probe quoted verbatim -- scripts/check-skip-ratchet.sh refuses a command that no file under scripts/ runs, so this record cannot invent a precondition nobody measures -- and `standing-gap` (the check's inputs ARE present and it still cannot assess, so it must name the OPEN issue that tracks it and is STALE the moment it assesses -- the entry must then be deleted). An entry that matters is matched EXACTLY (check + kind + the declared precondition, or the issue), so it cannot widen to cover a different blindness.

entries.reason: `CANNOT-ASSESS REQUIRED-BUT-UNOBSERVED` / `REQUIRED-BUT-GATED-OFF` -- branch protection REQUIRES `ao/gate-of-record` (#1342), the only producers on a PR verdict path (infra/cloudbuild/verify.yaml, the fleet runner rung) ship flag-gated OFF, and so no status is ever present on the commit under test; the check names this rather than passing (#1357). Its inputs ARE present in every venue that can run `gh auth status`, so this is not a venue gap: it is the open gap #1382 tracks (nothing on the ordinary lane path produces the required context). In the Cloud Build venue the same check answers `gh-unauthenticated: gh is not installed` (#1361), also rc 2. This entry goes STALE the moment a promoted producer posts the status and the check assesses -- delete it then.

`CANNOT-ASSESS CMR_VALIDATOR_UNAVAILABLE: vendor/CMR/sync/validate-cmr-pin.py not present (vendor/CMR submodule not initialized?)` -- in Cloud Build the submodule cannot be initialised offline (`fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'`), so this path is absent there and present in every worktree (#1361).
`check-cmr-pin: CANNOT-ASSESS -- vendor/CMR/sync/validate-cmr-pin.py not present (vendor/CMR submodule not initialized?)` -- the same absent precondition as cmr-knowledge (#1361).
`check-codeidx-surface: CANNOT-ASSESS - vendored mandatory seed unreadable: vendor/CMR/templates/module/.mcp.json (initialise vendor/CMR)` -- named by the check itself (#1361).

`check-diagrams-declaration: CANNOT-ASSESS - vendored contract unreadable: .../architecture-manifest.schema.json, .../gdc-manifest.schema.json, .../templates/module/gdc-manifest.yaml (initialise vendor/CMR)` -- the first of the three paths the check names (#1361).

`CANNOT-ASSESS compose-plugin-missing: install the docker compose v2 plugin (docker compose version must succeed)` -- and that is the probe this entry declares, verbatim from the check's own guard (scripts/check-fleet-cron-dev-run.sh). The Cloud Build container installs no docker (#1361).

`check-fleet-cron-image: CANNOT-ASSESS -- docker not found; the live controls were not run` (the declared-surface half is green; the live half is unreachable). `docker info` is the check's own probe of the daemon (scripts/check-fleet-cron-image.sh), supplied only when docker AND a reachable daemon are (#1361).

`CANNOT-ASSESS REQUIRED-BUT-GATED-OFF` -- the rc->state mapping and the poster are asserted and sound, and a producer exists on the PR verdict path, but that trigger ships flag-gated OFF (`disabled: true`, #1350) so nothing produces `ao/gate-of-record` until it is promoted out of band; the LIVE status is therefore never observable and the check refuses to call that a pass (#1357). Not a venue gap: `gh auth status` succeeds here and the check still cannot assess. The open issue that tracks the producer gap is #1382; in Cloud Build the same check is `gh-unauthenticated` (#1361), also rc 2. STALE the moment the check assesses -- delete it then.
`check-module-brief: CANNOT-ASSESS -- the pinned hub catalog is absent; expected vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv and vendor/CMR/catalog/modules` -- named by the check itself (#1361).

`check-module-registry: CANNOT-ASSESS -- the pinned hub catalog is absent; expected vendor/CMR/catalog/mandatory.tsv and vendor/CMR/catalog/modules` -- the venue case this record documented from the start, now naming the open issue that tracks the CI half (#1361).

`check-reconcile-orphans: CANNOT-ASSESS -- gh not found; orphan-pr / orphan-issue-lane / orphan-directive cannot be measured on the real tree` -- `command -v gh` is the check's OWN guard (scripts/check-reconcile-orphans.sh), supplied only in a venue that has gh. The Cloud Build venue installs no gh (#1361). Measured 2026-09-19: three independent heads (a4919733, 81f8d3ff, 4b9a8488) all answered `verify: FAIL (0 of 215 checks failed, 13 skipped ... skip ratchet FAIL: 1 unnamed skip)` for this one unmapped skip, so no pull request could pass control-plane-verify (#1405).

`CANNOT-ASSESS gh-unauthenticated: gh is not installed` -- the same shared precondition library as branch-protection (scripts/lib/preconditions.sh, required by scripts/check-repo-settings.sh) (#1361).

`check-worktree-cap: CANNOT-ASSESS -- reaper schedule could not be determined: prune-worktrees: schedule: CANNOT-ASSESS -- crontab -l failed with rc=127: ... crontab: command not found`. The reaper's schedule is read from the LIVE crontab, by design (scripts/prune-worktrees.sh), so with no `crontab` binary the question cannot be answered at all. `crontab -l` is that probe quoted verbatim (#1361).

why-these-entries-exist: The list holds ONLY the gaps of the CLOUD BUILD venue (#1361) and no local one, and that is a measurement, not an omission. In the two venues a DEVELOPER produces, nothing skips: (a) a FRESH WORKTREE (`git worktree add` of this repo) was run end to end -- 202 checks rc 0, 1 check rc 1 (an unrelated `reconcile` real-tree drift baseline), 0 checks rc 2, verdict `verify: FAIL (1 of 203 checks failed)` with NO `skipped:` clause at all; (b) the populated checkout of the same commit. A skip that appears on the developer box is therefore a FINDING, not a known limit, and the ratchet refuses it by name with the remedy printed beside it -- which is the property this issue asked for: a skip bucket that cannot be permanently populated. Every entry that IS in this record is one of the required check's runner's own gaps: `control-plane-verify (purebliss-ghl)` runs `make verify` inside a bare `python:3.14` container with no `gh`, no docker (so no compose v2 plugin), no `crontab`, and no network with which to initialise `vendor/CMR`, so those twelve checks answer rc 2 there on EVERY run. That is filed as #1361, the open issue each entry names; supplying the tool or repairing the check deletes the entry, and a stale entry fails the run by name. Each of them is an `unused_venue_entry` on every local run -- a NOTE, never a failure -- and bites only in the venue whose precondition is genuinely absent.

The two checks that used to occupy the bucket are NOT here because they were REPAIRED, not because they were excused: `dispatch-queue` (#1189) and `paperclip-routines` (#1176) both reach real verdicts (measured at origin/master a60ab88: rc 0 each, 9 and 11 controls provoked). Naming them would be the fiction this ratchet exists to prevent.

The `venue` KIND is not hypothetical and was measured too: in a tree carrying no local submodule objects (so `git submodule update --init vendor/CMR` cannot succeed offline), `module-registry`, `diagrams-declaration` and `codeidx-surface` each answer rc 2 -- `the pinned hub catalog is absent` / `vendored contract unreadable` / `vendored mandatory seed unreadable` -- exactly as each check's own header declares. A lane in that venue names them with the precondition path it is missing, or supplies the submodule; it does not get a silent PASS.

Growing this list is a deliberate act naming the PRECONDITION the venue lacks -- a repo-relative PATH, or a COMMAND the venue must be able to run -- together with the OPEN issue that tracks supplying it (#1361 for the Cloud Build container); shrinking it is automatic -- an entry whose check assesses FAILS the run until the entry is deleted.
